section_summary: This section contains a Department of State press release reproducing Ambassador Katsuji Debuchi’s note announcing the completion of Tokyo’s reconstruction after the 1923 earthquake and expressing Japan’s gratitude for American assistance, together with Acting Secretary Joseph P. Cotton’s reply. It concludes with a cross-reference sheet concerning a presidential congratulatory message for the fiftieth anniversary of the Japanese newspaper Jiji Shimpo and its recent goodwill mission to the United States.

subfiles.about: Publishes Japan’s appreciation for American aid after the 1923 earthquake and the Acting Secretary of State’s acknowledgment following the completion of Tokyo’s reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Katsuji Debuchi reports that reconstruction of Tokyo following the earthquake of September 1, 1923, has been completed and that March 26 was designated for a celebration. On behalf of Japan, he thanks the United States government and people for their sympathy, relief, encouragement, and cooperation. Acting Secretary Joseph P. Cotton replies that the American response was a spontaneous expression of the longstanding friendship between the two countries.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on the Jiji Shimpo fiftieth-anniversary message
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to Telegram No. 28 concerning the President’s congratulatory message to Jiji Shimpo on its fiftieth anniversary.
subfiles.summary: The sheet cross-references a telegram about a presidential congratulatory message sent to the Japanese newspaper Jiji Shimpo for its fiftieth anniversary. To avoid creating an awkward precedent, the message was framed as referring to the newspaper-sponsored goodwill mission recently sent to the United States.
